Vendored CCExtractor — provenance and inventory (WP4b, 2026-08-23)
=================================================================

Source (official release, x64):
  Release:      CCExtractor v0.96.6 (GitHub, published 2026-02-20)
  Asset:        CCExtractor.0.96.6_win_portable.zip (88,026,547 bytes)
  URL:          https://github.com/CCExtractor/ccextractor/releases/download/v0.96.6/CCExtractor.0.96.6_win_portable.zip
  Zip SHA-256:  c9b14cd356c7ada66b294426ba25c52d7654396a31b8b115b789e4d5e73f62bc
  Self-reports: CCExtractor 0.96.5, git 185631dcb0217b4ad09d43009cb69f0593996a5d
                (the v0.96.6 tag ships binaries stamped 0.96.5; verified
                byte-identical to the local MSI install of the same tag)

Why only these files: the zip is a Flutter-GUI distribution (221 MB
uncompressed). The CLI is ccextractorwinfull.exe, whose only
non-system static import is libgpac.dll; libgpac eagerly imports the
ffmpeg DLL set below, so the Windows loader requires all of them at
process start (verified: exe alone and exe-minus-one-DLL both fail
with exit 127; the full set below runs). Deliberately NOT vendored:
  tessdata/          only needed to OCR DVB-subtitle bitmaps — the app
                     never uses that path (see live_cc.ccx_args:
                     --no-codec dvbsub forces the CEA-608 SEI path)
  ccxgui.exe, flutter_windows.dll, data/, *_plugin.dll
                     the GUI and its assets
  msvcp140.dll, vcruntime140_1.dll
                     not in the import closure (GUI-only)

Layout note: the DLLs sit next to the exe in this folder; the Windows
loader searches the executable's own directory first, so the dev tree,
the PyInstaller _MEIPASS extraction, and a dist/ folder drop all work
without PATH setup.

License: CCExtractor is GPL-2.0-or-later. The portable zip ships no
license file of its own, so COPYING-ccextractor.txt in this folder
carries the GNU GPL v2 text (as before). Upstream source:
https://github.com/CCExtractor/ccextractor (LICENSE.GPLv2)

Replaced: the static CCExtractor 0.88 win build (ccextractorwin.exe,
1.9 MB) — it rejected every long CLI flag and its live pipeline was
fail-fasted in live_cc.CCSource.start (it could not serve the
--stdin/--stdout streaming topology).
